bug_semantics: During CRI container or sandbox creation, containerd copied every untrusted OCI/Docker image-config LABEL into the container's labels. An attacker-controlled image could therefore set containerd's reserved control labels, including containerd.io/restart.status/policy and containerd.io/restart.loguri. The restart monitor consumed loguri as trusted control metadata; a binary:// URI reached the shim's NewBinaryIO/NewBinaryCmd path, where exec.Command(binaryURI.Path, args...) launched the attacker-selected host binary as the host-root containerd/shim context.
flaw_origin: Commit f40df3d72ba85700c737aca2cb21212d8f0caaed expanded CRI buildLabels to accept image.ImageSpec.Config.Labels and blindly copy each imageConfigLabels entry before overlaying CRI-request labels, while also adding WithImageConfigLabels for ctr. It crossed the image-to-runtime-control trust boundary without excluding the containerd.io/* or io.cri-containerd* namespaces.
ai_marker: absent — the exact BIC commit object names author and committer Phil Estes <estesp@gmail.com>; its only message trailer is "Signed-off-by: Phil Estes <estesp@amazon.com>". It has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, other AI trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-xhf5-7wjv-pqxp states that CRI propagated image-config LABEL values without validation, allowing a plugin consuming container labels to execute an arbitrary host command, and identifies patched releases 1.7.33, 2.0.10, 2.1.9, 2.2.5, and 2.3.2. The repository's first-party docs/security/THREAT_MODEL.md CRI-004 names the concrete reserved label containerd.io/restart.loguri, binary:// interpretation, and host-root execution.

Source-history proof: `git log -L 283,301:pkg/cri/server/helpers.go f40df3d72ba85700c737aca2cb21212d8f0caaed` attributes the added `buildLabels(configLabels, imageConfigLabels, ...)` signature and `for k, v := range imageConfigLabels` loop to https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/f40df3d72ba85700c737aca2cb21212d8f0caaed. Cross-path `git log --all -S'image.ImageSpec.Config.Labels'` and `-S'for k, v := range imageConfigLabels'` found that original plus 6bfd09f7c91c042a2ce6c2a1025c88e2975395b6, whose commit object explicitly says it was cherry-picked from f40df3d72ba85700c737aca2cb21212d8f0caaed and whose containment is limited to v1.5.6-v1.5.18; later 2023-2024 hits are moves/renames/deduplication, not introductions.

BIC paths and lines: f40df3d72ba85700c737aca2cb21212d8f0caaed changes pkg/cri/server/helpers.go to copy imageConfigLabels without a namespace check and changes pkg/cri/server/container_create.go and pkg/cri/server/sandbox_run.go to pass image.ImageSpec.Config.Labels. It also introduces container_opts.go WithImageConfigLabels. Review diff: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/f40df3d72ba85700c737aca2cb21212d8f0caaed.

Direct-parent verification: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/d081457ba486b7c5c1e9f218f755b038061d90bc is the sole parent. `git show d081457...:pkg/cri/server/helpers.go` shows `buildLabels(configLabels map[string]string, containerType string)` and only `for k, v := range configLabels`; `git show ...:pkg/cri/server/container_create.go` shows `buildLabels(config.Labels, containerKindContainer)`. A tree-wide `git grep` at that parent for `image.ImageSpec.Config.Labels`, `WithImageConfigLabels`, and `imageConfigLabels` over the affected CRI/client paths returned no matches (exit 1). Thus the vulnerable image-label flow is absent in the direct parent.

Sink-at-introduction proof: `git grep` in the BIC tree finds runtime/restart/restart.go defining LogURILabel as `containerd.io/restart.loguri`, runtime/restart/monitor/monitor.go:225 assigning `labels[restart.LogURILabel]` to startChange.logURI, pkg/process/io.go:249 defining NewBinaryIO, and pkg/process/io_util.go:38 calling `exec.Command(binaryURI.Path, args...)`. These establish that the dangerous consumer already existed when the BIC made image labels reach it.

Affected-boundary proof: `git tag --contains f40df3d...` includes v1.6.0 and v1.7.0, so the BIC predates the advisory's first affected boundary. Tree checks find the unfiltered imageConfigLabels loop/call in v1.7.0 and v1.7.32, v2.0.0 and v2.0.9, v2.1.0 and v2.1.8, v2.2.0 and v2.2.4, and v2.3.0 and v2.3.1, matching the advisory ranges >=1.7.0,<1.7.33; >=2.0.0,<2.0.10; >=2.1.0,<2.1.9; >=2.2.0,<2.2.5; and >=2.3.0,<2.3.2.

Direct fix https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/0ec1af4cae1256d18719ca892bf66340499e8050 adds labels.IsReserved and skips image labels prefixed `containerd.io/` or `io.cri-containerd` in internal/cri/util.BuildLabels and client.WithImageConfigLabels. Stable backports and containment are: 4d8ba4d23561c9ec21b0113ddcfc22f41792b25e -> v1.7.33; bbf4a2b8e6c89483ff1b631f5814197fc8d99a0c -> v2.0.10; b6072a49f8d3f6efc5ac9895efbb1852b16a2602 -> v2.1.9; 429bcb924c278571f3d135933f562a87af1b6a53 -> v2.2.5; f99aad54af507168a1393dfae1559fde4cae9b2c -> v2.3.2. `git grep IsReserved(k)` succeeds in every first-patched tag, while each preceding tag retains the unfiltered loop.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p f40df3d72ba85700c737aca2cb21212d8f0caaed` produced parent d081457ba486b7c5c1e9f218f755b038061d90bc, human author/committer Phil Estes, a GPG signature, subject/body, and only the Signed-off-by trailer quoted in ai_marker. The 2026 fix commit has `Assisted-by: Claude Code`, but the protocol excludes fix-only AI attribution from the BIC judgment.
reasoning: The advisory and first-party threat model identify an untrusted-image-label-to-host-command control flow. Line history and pickaxe searches reduce its origin to f40df3d72ba85700c737aca2cb21212d8f0caaed: that commit simultaneously introduced the image-config argument, the unconditional copy loop, and the CRI call sites that supplied image labels. Its direct parent accepts and copies only CRI-request labels, and exact vulnerable identifiers are absent from that parent tree. The same-mechanism 6bfd09f7c91c042a2ce6c2a1025c88e2975395b6 explicitly identifies itself as a cherry-pick of f40df3d... and is therefore not a smaller/original BIC; later source hits merely move or deduplicate the already-vulnerable code. The dangerous restart/binary logger sink is present in the BIC tree. Tag-tree checks reproduce every advisory vulnerable/fixed boundary, and direct fix 0ec1af4cae1256d18719ca892bf66340499e8050 plus its five stable backports filters precisely the reserved namespaces that enabled the control-label injection. Finally, the exact BIC object has no AI authorship/co-authorship marker. Claude assistance appears only on the 2026 fix, so BIC-only attribution requires NOT_AI.
